destinations.title: Destinations
destinations.subtitle: From stilt-house villages to national parks, discover the exceptional diversity of Benin

items.description: The Venice of Africa, a unique stilt village on the water
items.longDescription: Ganvié is an exceptional lake village on Lake Nokoué. With 30,000 inhabitants living in stilt houses, it is the largest lake settlement in Africa. Life is organised entirely on the water: floating markets, schools, places of worship. Residents travel by pirogue in a fascinating aquatic ballet.

items.description: One of the last great wildlife sanctuaries in West Africa
items.longDescription: Pendjari National Park is a conservation jewel of West Africa. Over 275,000 hectares, it shelters exceptional wildlife: lions, elephants, buffalo, hippos, cheetahs and more than 300 bird species. The Tanougou waterfall and the Atacora mountains add to the beauty of the place.

items.description: Spiritual heart of vodun and memory of the slave trade
items.longDescription: Ouidah is a city steeped in history. The Slave Route and the Door of No Return bear witness to the tragedy of the slave trade. The town is also the cradle of vodun, with the Temple of Pythons and the Sacred Forest of Kpassè. Every January 10, the National Vodun Festival draws thousands of pilgrims.

items.description: The royal palaces of Dahomey, a World Heritage site
items.longDescription: Abomey was the capital of the mighty Kingdom of Dahomey for nearly 300 years. The royal palaces, a UNESCO World Heritage site, are adorned with exceptional bas-reliefs that tell the story of the kingdom. The historical museum holds priceless treasures: thrones, weapons, ritual objects.

items.description: Fine sand beaches, traditional fishing and a relaxed atmosphere
items.longDescription: Grand-Popo is a peaceful seaside resort where the Mono river meets the Atlantic Ocean. Its long palm-fringed beaches invite relaxation. The fishing village keeps its traditions. The Bouche du Roy offers magnificent landscapes.

items.description: The vibrant economic capital, between tradition and modernity
items.longDescription: Cotonou is the beating heart of Benin. This dynamic city blends modernity and tradition. Dantokpa market, one of the largest in West Africa, is a total immersion in local life. Place de l'Étoile Rouge, Notre-Dame cathedral and Fidjrossè beach are all worth discovering.

items.description: Gateway to Somba country and its tata houses
items.longDescription: Natitingou is the main town of Somba country, famed for its unique traditional homes: the tatas. These miniature mud fortresses look like small castles. The region offers magnificent landscapes of hills and valleys.

items.description: The administrative capital, rich in history and traditions
items.longDescription: Porto-Novo, the capital of Benin, is a city with a rich historical heritage. The Honmè Museum (former royal palace), the Afro-Brazilian style Great Mosque and the Garden of Plants and Nature are all worth a visit.
